signals.snippet: ACC supports 2.04 million new injury claims in 50th year — Annual Report 2023/24. Total cost $7.38B, treatment $4B.
ACC paid out $8.23 billion for 2,295,685 claims over the 2024/25 financial year — an 11.5% increase from last year, despite claims rising only 1.8%. Average claim cost $3,585.
ACC's Outstanding Claims Liability (OCL) rose $3.3 billion to $63.6 billion. June 2026 Monthly Turnaround Plan Report shows mixed results against 2025/26 targets.
In 2025, ACC spent $4.4 billion on treatment and rehabilitation and $3.1 billion on weekly compensation for more than 160,000 people unable to work.
Injury statistics – work-related claims: 2022. A total of 222,300 work-related claims were made in 2022 (down 5,200 from 2021).
ACC Injuries in New Zealand report: In 2025, sport and recreation injuries resulted in over 480,000 claims, leading to 2.5 million days of weekly compensation, $1 billion in lost productivity.
Rugby union: 58,045 claims at a cost of $155 million. Football: 47,860 claims at a cost of $86 million. (2025 winter sport injury claims)
ACC burn claims hit their highest level in five years — more than 20,000 burns-related injury claims in 2025, total recovery cost exceeding $40 million.
Cavadino et al. (2025): The age-standardised rate of ACC claims for unintentional injury was 46% higher among non-Māori (95% CI 44% to 48%) than Māori — equity access gap.
ACC provides comprehensive, no-fault personal injury cover for all New Zealand residents and visitors. ACC's role is to help prevent injuries and support recovery.
ACC publicly released its Turnaround Plan in January 2026. Combined new-year costs for 2025/26 are pegged at $2,556 million; plan target is $2 billion.
2026/27 Turnaround Plan released to lock in progress. ACC's long-term claims pool fell by 95 people in 2025/26. To reach the June 2027 target, ACC needs a fall of at least 954.
